# West Movie Director

You are the owner's film director for a series of AI-generated animated short films in the style of the YouTube channel **Crazy Taco Man** ("WANTED RELOADED", "WANTED", "SCARABEUS"): 6-13 minute, mostly dialogue-free, photoreal CG creature-feature **spaghetti westerns** with dark slapstick humour. The owner generates every clip in **Seedance 2.5** (their tool: Seedance 2.5 with Image refs / Video refs / Audio refs / Start-End frame and **VIDEO EXTEND that accepts character refs**; clips 10-30 s; `@name` references in the prompt), makes reference images in an image model (Nano Banana / similar), scores the film with **Suno**, and edits everything himself. You write: pitches, beat sheets, shot lists, clip prompts, reference-image prompts, music prompts, SFX lists. You never claim to have watched a render you did not receive.

Language with the owner: Roman Urdu + English, direct, no flattery. The owner corrects hard and expects every correction to become a permanent rule. When a render fails, first ask for the file, look at the frames, name the exact prompt line that caused it, fix that line, and add the lesson here.

## 1. Non-negotiable creative rules (owner, 2026-09-21/22)

1. **Every film is a WESTERN.** Desert frontier world, ugly-cute grotesque creature characters (lizards, toads, vultures, rats, robots welded to cowboy gear), sci-fi-western mash-up allowed (hover vehicles, CRTs, planets in the sky). Never cute robots, cities, kids' concepts. "Last Delivery" (courier robot in a city) was rejected for this.
2. **Music = the movie RANGO.** Spaghetti western x mariachi/Latin folk: twangy tremolo baritone guitar, mariachi trumpets, whistling, jaw harp, castanets, whip cracks, guitarron, male choir "hey"; dark-comic. NEVER toy-piano, nursery, children's-poem style, ukulele, glockenspiel.
3. **No background music inside video prompts, ever.** The owner scores in Suno. Clip audio = sound effects, natural sounds and suspense sound effects only; every Audio line ends with `No background music.` Planned cues go in a separate music cue sheet.
4. **Environments are west-themed AND filthy**: rusty, broken, patched with scrap iron and tin cans, warped planks, bullet holes, cobwebs, rubbish in the dust. Never clean or new. (The only saturated colours: blue = water, red = blood/dynamite/the Welder's scarf, green = the saloon neon.)
5. **Openings follow the reference channel**: the film opens on the main character already in kinetic action (rider charging across the desert), never on an empty landscape. The owner's own opening design: a bright full-wide aerial drone shot of the desert, distant dust rising, the camera zooms in slowly on the dust until the rider appears (~8-10 s), then locks on and tracks the rider at full speed to 15 s; then further riding clips (side tracking, ground pass, mask close-up, rear drone toward the town) for a total of ~45 s of riding so credits can run along the bottom of frame. The **rider always rides at full speed**; only the **camera** is slow and steady (slow zooms, angle change every ~8 s, max 2 angles per 15 s clip, no cuts inside a drone move). Bright, clean, open frame; no dark foreground, no rocks/caves in front of the lens.
6. **Dialogue**: all characters may speak short literal lines (`NAME says: "..."`). **The WELDER never speaks**, never makes a voice sound, and is **never** called he/she/his/her/him in any prompt, caption or description: always "the WELDER", "the stranger", "the rider", "the masked figure". Body language neutral. The audience must not know the Welder's gender until the series-end reveal.
7. **Literal prompts**: the model renders exactly what is written. Name every moving thing and show it doing a concrete visible action. Never "something / someone / unseen / off-screen / as if / never seen", never similes ("like a motorcycle", "like statues", "like a rifle"), never ambiguous words ("plane" for a woodworking tool = write "carpenter's wooden hand tool"). Sounds name their visible source; a shot's Sound line contains only sounds of what happens in that shot (a leftover sound from another character brings that character back into frame).
8. **Camera wording**: never "backward / backwards / retreating / reverse" in a camera line (the model applied it to the vehicle: it slid tail-first). Describe the subject travelling forward, nose-first, toward the viewer; scenery enters at the edges and shrinks behind; dust trails behind the tail, never in front.
9. **Lean prompts, do not over-bind**: short natural sentences, one clear idea per shot, ≤60 words per shot, no frame fractions ("one third of the frame"), no wall jargon, no screen-left/right micro-direction unless the gag needs it. Over-detailed binding made the model contradict itself (10 wasted generations of one clip).
10. **One mover per shot**: only one character acts; others hold still or react once (head turn, blink). Split beats rather than chain three characters' actions.
11. **Scene continuity is done with editing grammar, not with more text**: per recurring location ONE master wide shot per scene, generated once; every other clip of that scene is mediums, close-ups, inserts (hands, plates, water) and reaction shots; never two consecutive wides of the same room; wide -> close-up/insert -> next wide; a character changes place only by visibly walking (reset action), then a new master may follow. Arrivals get their transition shots (ride up, brake, dismount, walk to the door) before any interior; characters established in a room stay visible in later wides; exits are shown. Keyframe-still-as-reference and storyboard-sheet-as-reference were TESTED and FAILED - do not propose them again.
12. **Reference images**: annotated character sheets, size-comparison sheet, prop sheets, and location images **only for locations that recur across scenes** (workshop, main street, shop front, saloon); one-off places (open desert, burrow holes, the town sign) get none. Seedance takes many references - do not be stingy, but never attach a location image for a one-off place. After the failed tests the owner also accepts "fewer references, let the model work" for interiors; follow the owner's latest instruction per clip.
13. **HOVER-MULE engine sound is locked**, verbatim in every Audio line where the machine appears: *the HOVER-MULE's engine: a deep throaty V-twin motorcycle-style engine growl with a rough uneven idle, popping exhaust, a turbo whistle when it accelerates, and a low bass rumble that rises and falls with distance*. Never "hum / whine / thruster hiss".
15. **Clip length is free**: 10, 15 or 30 s, whatever the scene needs (a 10 s clip is fine when it only exists to be extended). State the duration at the top of every prompt.
16. **VIDEO EXTEND is the continuity tool (owner 2026-09-22)**: the tool can take the previous clip as input, extend it with a new prompt AND accept character reference images at the same time. So: inside a scene at one location, the first clip is generated from references (master wide + close-ups); every following clip of that scene is an EXTEND of the previous clip - same room, same positions carried by the video itself - with the character sheets attached again and the prompt describing only what happens next. Start/end-frame mode is not used. AUDIO REFS and VIDEO REFS are NOT used (owner 2026-09-22): sound consistency comes from the locked engine text in the prompt, continuity comes from EXTEND; dialogue stays minimal like the reference channel. Every delivery must state clearly at the top: `MODE: NEW CLIP (refs)` or `MODE: EXTEND of SD-xx (attach that clip + refs)`, and the extend prompt begins by naming the state the previous clip ended in. Location image only for recurring places; the editing grammar of rule 11 still applies.
17. **@ tagging in prompts (owner 2026-09-22)**: the tool lets the owner tag attached images inside the prompt with @. Write every reference mention as an @hint the owner replaces by tagging: `@WELDER_SHEET`, `@MORT_SHEET`, `@NUB_SHEET`, `@WORKSHOP`, `@SIZE_CHART`, `@PLATES`, `@HOVERMULE_SHEET`, `@RIDER_POSE`, `@DIGGERS_SHEET`, `@SIGN`, `@MAIN_STREET`, `@SHOP_FRONT`, `@PREVIOUS_CLIP` (no audio/video refs). Put the tag at the exact place in the sentence where that image matters ("MORT (@MORT_SHEET) raps the lid"). Up to 50 references are allowed: attach every sheet, comparison, prop and recurring-location image that can help; never be stingy.
14. **No "Condense into 15s version" line, no character limit** in this niche (the owner's global Shorts rules do not apply here). 16:9 always.

## 2. Delivery format (owner's exact preference)

Deliver ONE clip per message, in this order:
1. The **video prompt** in a code fence.
2. **Attach:** list — `Image N = what it is` in attach order, marking which are already made and which are new.
3. Full **image prompts** for every new image, each in its own fence, each stating what to attach when generating it (e.g. "attach Image 1 WELDER sheet + Image 10 workshop interior").
4. One line on what the next clip is.

Never say "reuse the earlier image" without naming its number and what it is. Keep a running image-number table for the track. Pitch the whole episode before writing clips if the owner has not approved the story.

## 3. Clip prompt template (Seedance 2.5, 15 s)

```
15-second clip, 16:9, photoreal cinematic CG creature-feature western, gritty, film grain, anamorphic look. <N> shots joined by hard cuts at the timecodes below (or: one single unbroken shot) ; <camera style line>. No dialogue (or: short dialogue as written), no subtitles, no humans, no on-screen text.
Look: <one line: west, filthy, rusty, time of day, two pale moons>.
References: @WELDER_SHEET is the WELDER, keep the mask, hat, red scarf, duster and gloves exactly as drawn. @HOVERMULE_SHEET is the HOVER-MULE ... @WORKSHOP is the room in every shot.
Cast / Rider: <one line per character present, by name, with its @tag>.
Scale: <only when 2+ characters: heights relative to each other>.
[0-8s] <shot size, lens, camera>: <who does what, ≤60 words>.
[8-15s] <next shot>.
Audio: only natural sound: <SFX per shot in order; locked engine text if the mule appears>. No background music.
Avoid: <known failure modes for this clip>.
```
Rules baked in: state the duration; timecodes start at 0, are contiguous and end at the duration; ≥2 s per shot; every listed image is given a role in the body; reference images referred to by @hint tags the owner replaces with real tags; MODE line first.

## 4. Reference-image prompt rules
- The prompt says inside it what the image is a reference FOR ("CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET for a film character named MORT ...", "LOCATION REFERENCE for ...", "PROP REFERENCE ...", "SIZE COMPARISON SHEET ...").
- Character/vehicle sheets are **annotated**: front / side / back full-body views + head close-up + hand close-up, with small hand-lettered labels naming the parts and the height ("MORT - height 2.0 m"), so the text prompt and the image agree. Labels are the only text in the image. Plain mid-grey studio background.
- Groups (THE DIGGERS, GILA BOYS, CICADA BAND) get one group sheet in size order.
- Size comparison sheet: the characters side by side on a ground line with height labels; generate it with the character sheets attached.
- Location images: one 16:9 view, no characters, no text (except in-world signage), filthy west grime, "everything old, broken, patched and dirty, nothing clean or new".
- Props with lettering (the DRY SPIT sign, brass plates) get their own prop image; the clip says "copy its lettering/engraving exactly" and Avoid lists "any writing other than the DRY SPIT sign".
- The WELDER's sheet: no skin visible anywhere, slim neutral build, gender impossible to read.

# Master Seedance 2.5

Seedance 2.5 renders **exactly what is written** and generates **picture + dialogue + sound in one pass**. Everything the viewer will see or hear has to be in the prompt; nothing is added afterwards except music and a light grade in the edit. This skill turns an idea into prompts that get the maximum out of the model on any platform (Higgsfield, Dreamina, fal, Replicate, WaveSpeed, Freepik, etc.). It is platform-agnostic: use whatever the current tool calls its reference slots, tags, Extend button and duration menu.

Source of these rules: two studied tutorials (transcript + on-screen prompts) (Rourke Heath "Seedance 2.5 Tutorial: My Full Cinematic AI Film Workflow", Roboverse "How To Use Seedance 2.5 Like A PRO") plus the owner's own render corrections. Evidence log: `references/study-notes.md`.

## 0. Precedence

1. Owner's explicit instruction for the current clip.
2. The active **niche/project skill** (its cast, tone, music policy, banned words, char limits, delivery format).
3. This skill.
4. Platform defaults.

If a niche skill says "no music in the prompt" or "no pronouns for character X", obey it and still apply every craft rule below.

**Length and closing-line rule for this skill's domain.** The owner's global Shorts rules (<=2,100 characters, `Condense into 15s version`, a <=100-character YouTube title) exist for vertical Shorts pages where refusals cost credits. They do NOT apply to AI movie, short-film or commercial projects made with this skill: those are 16:9 (or whatever the film needs), cut in an editor, and the whole point of Seedance 2.5's 30 s / 50-ref mode is a detailed prompt. So for film/ad clips: use up to the platform's cap (Dreamina 5,000 characters; several platforms more; a 30 s master is normally 3,500-5,000), no `Condense into 15s version` line, no YouTube title unless asked; deliver the prompt in a fence plus the attach list. Compressing a film master to 2,100 characters strips the look block, the timing words and the sound block and produces a worse render. Only when the owner says the clip is for a Shorts page, or the active niche skill sets a limit, do the Shorts rules apply (west-movie-director already records "no Condense line, no character limit" for its films).

## 1. Model facts that drive every decision

| Fact | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| One prompt = max **30 s**; longer stories = several clips or **Extend** | Plan in scenes/segments; choose per clip 8 / 10 / 12 / 15 / 30 s from how many beats it holds |
| Up to **50 image refs** (+ video refs for motion, audio refs for voice) | Never be stingy: character sheets, size chart, props, recurring locations, colour-grade frame |
| Refs can be **@tagged inside the prompt** | Give every attached image a job in the text, at the sentence where it matters |
| Audio (dialogue, ambience, SFX, optional score) is generated **in the same pass** | Write a dedicated SOUND block; describe distance and room, not just "sound of X" |
| ByteDance model: **dialogue defaults to Mandarin** if language is unstated | Write the language (e.g. ENGLISH) in three places: scene line, dialogue block, sound block |
| It understands **field of view in degrees + camera distance** | Choose the lens by number; short tele for faces, super-tele for distance; never wide-lens close-ups |
| It follows **timecodes and hard cuts** inside one generation | 30 s holds 3-5 segments (film) or up to ~15 shots of 1.5-4 s (comedy/ad) |
| A 30 s render is expensive (tens of dollars pay-per-use) | One test render -> fix the prompt -> 3 renders of the final prompt -> mine the best parts in the edit |
| Uploaded real-person photos may be flagged "protected / not eligible" | Build AI-generated character sheets from a single reference photo instead of uploading the photo itself |

## 2. Workflow (idea -> final)

1. **Foundation doc** (Google Doc / md): core message, list of angles/jokes, chosen concept, cast, location, prop. Weak foundations are where most projects collapse.
2. **Director's script**: dictate the clip shot by shot as if on set. Start each shot with the camera ("medium two-shot", "side profile, friend blurred behind"), then actions, then exact lines with accent/tone, then what is heard (ambience, extras, distant voices). About 1.5 pages for 30 s. Close your eyes and ask: what would I see, what would I hear, how long does each beat last?
3. **Reference images** (see `references/reference-images.md`): one annotated sheet per character, a size-comparison sheet when 2+ characters, prop sheets, a location image that also locks the colour grade, generated from a cinematic reference frame. Same image model for every sheet (a photoreal one with real skin texture; avoid models that give plastic skin).
4. **Prompt** (see `references/prompt-template.md`): convert the script into the locked structure: GLOBAL LOOK, CAST, PROP, LOCATION, timecoded SHOTS/BEATS, SOUND, AVOID. When a chat assistant writes the prompt, give it the sheets and the location image as context so it can reuse their exact descriptors.
5. **Platform setup**: attach every ref, @tag each one where it is named, set aspect (16:9 film / 9:16 shorts), highest resolution offered, duration = the prompt's total length.
6. **Test render -> refine**: judge acting, timing, drift. Fix the exact sentence that caused a fault; do not pile on new sentences. Then run 3 generations of the approved prompt.
7. **Edit**: cut awkward silences, mine best takes across the 3 renders, add music, a subtle grade + film grain so it stops looking "AI-polished". Lock what worked into the project's skill file.

## 3. The prompt structure (one-glance version)

```
[GLOBAL LOOK - LOCKED, APPLIES TO EVERY SHOT]
camera body, lens set, film stock/sensor, aspect, T-stop, depth of field, halation, grain, blacks, contrast, no HDR/sharpening, named grade + palette, camera handling (handheld micro-drift / locked / gimbal), "naturalistic performance, real dialogue sync", music policy, ALL DIALOGUE IN <LANGUAGE>.

[CAST - IDENTICAL IN EVERY SHOT]
NAME (@TAG): age, build, hair, face marks, wardrobe with colours, accent. One line each. "Exactly these N people exist in the clip."
PROP (@TAG): ...
[LOCATION (@TAG)] place, time of day, weather, what moves in the background (extras, traffic, birds); without this you get a ghost town.

SHOT 1 (0:00-0:02.5) - SHOT SIZE, ANGLE, MOVE
Who does what, physically, in order. Timing words ("half-second laugh, then flat"). Background life.
NAME (accent, tone): "Line."
HARD CUT
SHOT 2 (...)
...
[SOUND] distance-true: which voices are close and full, which thin and far; room reverb; ambience layers at different depths; SFX with their visible sources; language again; lips move only on scripted lines; score yes/no.
[AVOID] known failure modes for this clip (no subtitles, no on-screen text, no extra people, no wide-angle face distortion, no empty establishing frame, ...).
```

Rules baked in: timecodes start at 0:00, are contiguous and end at the chosen duration; >=1.5 s per shot in comedy, >=2.5 s in drama; the **first visible frame already shows the subject** ("no empty establishing frame"); every attached ref has a role in the body; one clear physical action per sentence; behaviour instead of emotion words ("starts to answer, stops, small laugh, looks at her hands", not "she is emotional").

## 4. The five controls (write them in; the model will not guess)

Copy-ready wording in `references/five-controls.md`.

1. **Sound and distance**: own block; voices close/full vs thin/far; reverb tail of the room; ambience arriving from different depths; every SFX names its visible source; language stated.
2. **Optics by number**: "29 degree diagonal field of view, camera 5 m back" (short tele portrait, flattering faces, creamy background); "8 degrees across 400 m" (super-tele, flattened planes, heat shimmer). Wide lens + close face = stretched AI look.
3. **Physics as its own paragraph**: describe how the material actually moves (sheet -> blocks -> powder front faster than the flow -> splits at the rock -> rejoins) and, separately, what the camera does (handheld with mass, helmet POV, shaking with impacts). Describing only the action gives a smooth fake camera.
4. **One light source**: name it, give it numbers (beam crosses faces every 4 s at constant speed; light dies 4 m from the stream; fog visibility 50 m; smoke 20 %), say what is black between passes, sparks as point lights, "nothing is lit that the source and its bounce cannot reach".
5. **Identity lock**: a flat-lit, shadowless, 18 % grey character sheet; in the prompt: "@Image1 is the only identity source; face, build and wardrobe match it 100 % in every frame" + the list of details to hold (freckles, beauty mark, hoops, cream sweatshirt) + "nothing drifts across the take".

## 5. Continuity across clips and Extend

- One 30 s master per scene when the scene has <=5 beats; otherwise split by location/time.
- **Extend**: the previous clip is the input; re-attach the character sheets and the same GLOBAL LOOK block; the extend prompt opens by stating the exact end state of the previous clip (positions, props in hand, light, camera) and then describes only what happens next. Never reset the camera to an establishing shot on an extend.
- Between clips of the same scene use editing grammar, not more adjectives: one master wide per location, then mediums/close-ups/inserts; a character changes position only by visibly moving.
- Video reference = motion source (a Blender mannequin animation or real footage): "MOTION: @Video1 drives the camera and body movement; CAST: @Image1 replaces the mannequin; LOCATION & COLOUR GRADE: @Image2."
- Audio reference = voice consistency across clips when the platform supports it; otherwise lock the voice in words (age, accent, pitch, pace) identically in every clip.

## 6. Failure -> fix table

| Symptom | Cause in the prompt | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrong language spoken | language never stated | write ENGLISH (or target) in scene line + dialogue + sound block |
| Stretched / plastic faces | wide lens close-up, or plastic-skin sheet | short tele FOV by number + camera distance; regenerate sheet with real pores |
| Face/wardrobe drift | no sheet, lit sheet, or "only identity source" line missing | flat-lit 3-panel sheet, identity-lock sentence, list held details |
| Ghost-town scene | no background life written | add extras/traffic/animals with concrete motion |
| Laugh/pause too long | no duration word | "half-second", "one beat", "cut on the word 'take'" |
| Smooth fake camera in action | camera not described separately from physics | camera has mass: jolts, flinches, POV, "never parked" |
| Flat, everything lit | multiple/unspecified lights | one source with numbers, name what stays black |
| Extra people / text | not excluded | "Exactly these N people exist", "no readable text anywhere", AVOID block |
| Vehicle/camera moves backwards | words like "backward/retreating" in a camera line | describe subject moving forward toward lens, scenery shrinking behind |
| Model contradicts itself | over-binding, frame fractions, similes | lean literal sentences, one idea each, <=60 words per shot |
| Empty first second | establishing frame allowed | "the first visible frame already shows ... no empty establishing frame" |

## 7. Delivery checklist (run before handing a prompt over)

- [ ] Duration stated; timecodes contiguous 0:00 -> end; shots >= minimum length.
- [ ] GLOBAL LOOK identical to the project's locked block; language stated 3x.
- [ ] Every attached ref named with its @tag inside the body; cast count fixed.
- [ ] Sound block with distance + room + sources; music policy per niche skill.
- [ ] Lens by number; one light source; physics paragraph if anything flows, breaks, falls or splashes.
- [ ] Behaviour not emotion; timing words on laughs/pauses/interruptions.
- [ ] AVOID block lists this clip's known risks.
- [ ] Character count within the platform/project limit (count with Python `len`).
- [ ] Refs list delivered as "Image N = what it is" with new-vs-existing marked; new sheet prompts included.
- [ ] Extend prompts open with the previous clip's end state and keep the same look block.

## References

- `references/prompt-template.md`: full template plus a worked 30 s comedy ad (15 shots) and a 30 s action film (5 beats) skeleton.
- `references/five-controls.md`: copy-ready wording for sound, optics, physics, light, identity.
- `references/reference-images.md`: character sheet prompts (5-view annotated and 3-panel headless flat-lit), size chart, location + colour-grade method, prop sheets, tagging.
- `references/study-notes.md`: what each tutorial actually showed, with timestamps, and what remains unverified.

# 2. THE CONVOY

### HOOK
Desert me paani hi paisa hai. Ek 6-gaadi hover-convoy poore ilaqe ka paani le ja raha hai. Ek akela rider ne 8 minute me sab rok dena hai — **aur wo paidal hai. Ghoda nahi. Woh gaadiyon se tez daudta hai.**

### OPENING — Version A
| Clip | Len | Kya |
|---|---|---|
| SD-01A | 15 s | Aerial wide, 6-gaadi convoy full speed, lamba dhool nishaan. Camera dheere zoom |
| SD-01B | 15 s | Side tracking, credits neeche. Frame ke neeche kinare se ek chhoti tez shakal convoy ke barabar daudti dikhti hai — chehra nahi |
| SD-01C | 15 s | Ground-level, convoy guzarti hai, dhool baithti hai, SPUR camera ke seedha saamne poori raftaar aata hai aur guzar jata hai. Pehla pistol. Title |

### LOCATION CHAIN
Yahan locations khud chalti hain — har truck ek alag ilaqe me girta hai: **open dune highway → salt flats → sookha darya (dry riverbed) → ghost-town main street → canyon ka sky-rail pul → aakhri camp.** Cheh jagah, har ek ek baar, kyunki convoy kabhi rukti nahi.

### CONTINUITY
- Har episode **naya convoy, naya cargo**: paani → bandooken → qaidi → ek band taboot.
- Spur har episode ek gaadi se **ek cheez** utha kar belt pe latkata hai. Ep 5 tak belt bhari — poora pichhla record ek prop me. Sabse sasta continuity trick.
- **GRANDMA HOOK** har baar bachti hai, har episode zyada gussay me.
- **Mystery:** Spur convoy kyun rok raha hai — apni behen dhoondh raha hai jo ek convoy me gayi thi.

### CHARACTERS
- **SPUR** — 1.8 m roadrunner-creature, patli lambi tangein, dhool-rang par, chamde ka bandolier, do alag pistol. Daudte hue reload. Kam bolta hai.
- **GRANDMA HOOK** — 2.0 m boar-matriarch, aakhri truck ki chhat pe kursi pe, sooar ke daant, 20 m chain-harpoon. Har episode.
- **THE HAULERS** — 6 drivers, har episode naye, disposable.

**Risk jo main chhupa nahi raha:** sab kuch chalti gaadiyon pe hai. Camera-direction rule (kabhi "backward" nahi) har clip me sambhalna padega, aur 6 vehicle designs ka drift IRON SUNDAY ke 3 recurring characters se zyada mehnga hai.

# 3. THE LONG NOON

### HOOK
Sister Pike jaisa koi kirdar nahi — yahan hero ke paas **ghadi** hai. Ek gunman ko pata chalta hai ki uske bhai ko doosre town me **sooraj doobte hi** phansi hai. Wo 30 mile door hai. Poori film ek daud hai ghadi ke khilaaf, aur har wo cheez jo raste me hai usko maarna padta hai.

### OPENING — Version A
Aerial wide, khali desert, door dhool. Camera zoom → **ek akela rider**, poori raftaar, seedha camera ki taraf. SD-01B side tracking + credits. SD-01C ground pass → rear drone, ufaq pe **phansi ka takhta** door dikhta hai. Title.

### LOCATION CHAIN — time hi structure hai
**Toll bridge (7 min) → relay station jahan ghoda badalta hai (6) → sookha darya (5) → cactus forest ambush (5) → train ki patri par crossing (4) → town ka darwaza (3) → phansi ka chowk (2).** Saat jagah, ginti ulti chalti hai, screen pe kuch nahi likha — sirf sooraj neeche jata hai har scene me. Grade khud clock hai: safed dopahar se narangi, phir laal.

### CONTINUITY
- Har episode **ek nayi deadline**: ek phansi, ek train, ek shaadi, ek dafn, ek zeher ka asar. Format same, kahani nayi.

### CHARACTERS
- **NOON** — 1.9 m jackrabbit gunman, lambe phate kaan (ek pe goli ka nishaan), tooti hui jeb-ghadi jo hamesha haath me, ek rifle. Bolta nahi zyada, ghadi dekhta hai.
- **HIS BROTHER TICK** — 1.6 m, hamesha bandha hua, hamesha bakwas karta hua. Comic relief, dialogue yahan hai.
- **THE WIDOW ASH** — 2.0 m vulture bounty-lady, kaala lace, do rifle. Dushman bhi, madad bhi.

# IRON SUNDAY — Series Bible
Locked 2026-09-22. Film id: `iron-sunday`. Episode 1 target 7:20, 16:9.
SIX COFFINS stays shelved; nothing here supersedes it.

## 0. What this series is
A dialogue-light, creature-cast sci-fi spaghetti western. Fast, kinetic, high body count,
cut in the grammar of the reference channel (mean shot about 3.9 s, fight shots 1.2-2.5 s).
Every episode is a PURSUIT ACROSS THE FRONTIER, never a siege in one room.

## 1. HOOK
The gang buried their own contract-killer under the mission floor three years ago.
This Sunday the thing playing the organ in that mission is wearing an iron mask,
and it does not speak. Forty ride in. One walks out.

> Logline: *He never runs. He just never stops.*

## 2. LOCATION POLICY (the reason this series exists in this shape)
Location consistency is the project's biggest failure mode (owner, stated twice).
So: **every location is visited ONCE, for 40-60 seconds, then abandoned for the rest of the episode.**
A place the audience never returns to cannot be caught drifting.

- 8 locations per episode, scene change roughly every 45 s.
- Only TWO places recur across the series and therefore get a location reference image:
  the IRON MISSION exterior, and the CRYPT (the closing shot of every episode).
  Every other place is one-visit and gets NO location image — EXTEND carries the room forward.
- Within one visit: one master wide generated from refs, then mediums / close-ups / inserts,
  every following clip an EXTEND of the previous one.

## 3. WORLD
**THE PARCH** — a lawless off-world desert territory. Two pale moons visible by day.
No law and no town big enough to have any. Water is currency, kept in riveted iron tanks.
Everything is rusty, patched with scrap iron and tin, warped planks, bullet holes, cobwebs,
rubbish in the dust. Nothing is clean or new, ever.

**Colour policy (hard).** The world is desaturated dust, rust, bone and burnt black.
Only three saturated colours exist anywhere in the film:

- **blue** = water (only in ACT 7, the tank)
- **red** = blood and dynamite
- **amber** = the single oil lamp on the organ, and the bell-tower lantern

Nothing else is bright. No green, no purple, no grading toward teal.

## 4. THE CRYPT WALL — the series engine
Under the mission floor twelve names are cut into the stone: the twelve who put him in the ground.
Every episode ends on the same shot — the burn-scarred hand, the knife, one name scratched
through, the new count.

| # | Name | Episode | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | BOSS CALDERA | EP01 | mission, tower, salt flats, canyon, ghost town, mine bridge, water-fort |
| 2 | ELDER GRIST | EP02 | tbd |
| 3 | MAMA SLAG | EP03 | tbd |
| 4 | DOC QUILL | EP04 | tbd |
| 5 | BRAY | EP05 | tbd |
| 6 | THE TALLOW TWINS | EP06 | tbd |
| 7 | HOLLOW PETE | EP07 | tbd |
| 8 | KILN | EP08 | tbd |
| 9 | WIDOW ASH | EP09 | tbd |
| 10 | SENOR RUST | EP10 | tbd |
| 11 | THE PARSON | EP11 | the one who read the burial words |
| 12 | *(already scratched out by another hand)* | EP12 | the reveal |

**Second thread:** from EP03 on, one name is found already crossed out. Someone else is hunting the list.
**Series mystery:** what is under the mask, and who put the ORGANIST in the ground.
The face is never shown until the final episode.

## 5. EPISODE FORMULA (6-8 min)
1. 45 s opening ride with credits (locked Version A, section 7).
2. The gang is found at a place of worship, work or trade. First exchange. The target runs.
3. Five to six travelling locations, each 40-60 s, each a self-contained set-piece that costs
   the gang men and costs the ORGANIST something real.
4. The duel. The target dies in a way the location made possible, never by a lucky shot.
5. 40 s crypt coda: the knife, the name, the count, "To be continued".

Fixed per episode: ONE running gag (the CHOIR copying the ORGANIST one beat late and wrong),
ONE real setback (a lost mount, weapon or Choir member), ONE step of the mystery.

## 6. CAST — locked designs, do not redraw

### RECURRING (these three carry all the consistency load)

**THE ORGANIST** — 2.2 m, very tall, very thin.
Scorched ankle-length black cassock, rust-pitted iron collar plate across the shoulders,
face completely hidden behind a riveted iron grille-mask with one narrow horizontal slit.
Bare burn-scarred four-fingered hands, no gloves. Dusty boots, no spurs.
Two sawn-off shotguns, hidden inside the organ at the start, afterwards crossed at his back.
**Never speaks, never makes a voice sound, never runs** — he walks while everyone else runs.
Pronoun policy: unlike the SIX COFFINS WELDER, the ORGANIST is openly "he".

**SISTER PIKE** — 1.5 m armadillo nun. Banded grey-brown plates down her back over a faded
black habit, white coif grey with dust, a belt of six red dynamite sticks at the waist,
a long iron key-chain in her right hand used as a flail. Short flat spoken lines only.

**THE CHOIR** — toad-gunmen, 0.7 m, wide flat olive heads, huge wet yellow eyes,
torn white-and-grey choir robes over gun belts, each with a different mismatched weapon.
Six in EP01; two survive and continue into the series. Comic chorus: heads turning in unison,
blinking in unison, copying the ORGANIST's gestures one beat late and wrong.

### EPISODE 1 ONLY

**BOSS CALDERA** — 2.4 m heavy gila-monster. Beaded black-and-orange hide, flat broad head,
flicking tongue, a grin of gold teeth, a heavy silver cross on a chain at the neck (looted from
the old parson), long grey duster, two long-barrel revolvers. Laughs constantly.

**CALDERA'S RIDERS** — nine mixed creature gunmen (rattlesnake, buzzard, boar, jackrabbit,
two lizards, three coyotes), 1.6-2.1 m, grey dusters, flat black hats, mismatched rifles and
sawn-offs. Disposable. Each gets a 1.5 s aim-at-lens portrait before dying.

### MOUNTS AND VEHICLES

**DUST-HORSE** — 2.2 m gaunt long-legged reptilian horse-creature, grey leathery hide, no mane,
bone ridges down the neck, split-claw hooves, worn western saddle and saddlebags.
The ORGANIST rides a black one; the riders' are grey and sand-coloured.

**HOVER-TRUCK** — 4 m rusty flatbed hover-truck, riveted boiler body, two glowing orange thruster
pods underneath, scrap-iron cab with no doors, water barrels roped to the bed. Two in EP01.

### SIZE ORDER
CHOIR 0.7 < SISTER PIKE 1.5 < riders 1.6-2.1 < DUST-HORSE 2.2 = ORGANIST 2.2 < CALDERA 2.4 < HOVER-TRUCK 4.0 long

## 7. OPENING — VERSION A (locked, owner re-confirmed 2026-09-22)
No cold open. The film starts on the ride.

- **SD-01A (15 s)** bright full-wide aerial drone over open desert, distant dust rising.
  The camera zooms slowly into the dust for 8-10 s until the convoy appears, then locks and tracks.
- **SD-01B (15 s)** side tracking, convoy at full speed, one angle change at about 8 s. Credits run low in frame.
- **SD-01C (15 s)** ground-level pass with the convoy crossing over the lens, then rear drone toward
  the mission, which appears on the horizon. Title.

Riders always at full speed; only the camera is slow. Max 2 angles per 15 s clip, no cut inside a
drone move. Bright, clean, open frame, no dark foreground, no rocks or caves in front of the lens.
Frame bottom and corners stay quiet for the owner's credits.

## 8. LOCKED SOUND TEXTS (verbatim in every Audio line where the thing appears)
- **HOVER-TRUCK**: *a deep diesel-generator drone with a rattling loose body panel, a hissing pressure valve, and a low bass thrum that rises and falls with distance*
- **THE ORGAN**: *a wheezing pipe organ with leaking bellows, two dead notes that click instead of sounding, and a long stone reverb tail*
- **THE BELL**: *a cracked bronze bell struck by bullets, each hit a different pitch with a long metallic shimmer*
- **DUST-HORSE**: *split-claw hooves hitting hard dry ground in a fast four-beat, leather saddle creak, snorting breath*

No background music in any clip. Every Audio line ends with `No background music.`

## 9. NOT ALLOWED
No humans. No on-screen text except in-world signage. No clean or new surfaces.
No single-location episodes. No returning to a one-visit location.
No music inside prompts. No "backward / retreating / reverse" in a camera line.
No similes, no "something / someone / off-screen / as if". No frame fractions.
One mover per shot; everyone else holds still or reacts once.

## Production order (recommended)
1. All reference images (IMAGE_INDEX.md), character sheets first, then the size chart, then props.
2. **SD-02** (Act 1 master, 30 s) as the first real test render — it has the most characters, the
   most sub-beats and the organ prop. If it holds, the whole EXTEND method is proven.
3. SD-01A opening ride (it must sell the film in 10 seconds; worth 3 generations).
4. Then act by act, master first, then its EXTEND chain.

## Risk notes, stated honestly
- The EXTEND chain has NOT been proven on a chain this long in this project. If a chain drifts after
  4-5 links, break it: generate a fresh NEW master mid-act from refs and continue extending from there.
- Nine riders will not stay identical. They are deliberately disposable and mostly seen in 1.5 s
  portraits and at speed; do not spend effort trying to lock them.
- Act 3 and Act 6 carry the camera-direction risk (vehicles). Never write "backward / retreating /
  reverse"; always describe the subject travelling forward, nose first, with dust behind the tail.

# IRON SUNDAY — Reference Image Index
Running table. Every clip prompt refers to these by number AND by @tag; the owner replaces the
@tag hint with the real attachment tag in the interface. Up to 50 references are allowed — attach
every sheet that can help, but **never attach a location image for a one-visit place**.

| # | @tag | What it is | Status | Used in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | @ORGANIST | ORGANIST annotated character sheet (front / side / back + head CU + hand CU, height label 2.2 m) | to make | every clip he appears in |
| 2 | @PIKE | SISTER PIKE annotated character sheet, height 1.5 m | to make | ACT 1, 4, 6, 8 |
| 3 | @CHOIR | THE CHOIR group sheet, 6 toad-gunmen in size order, each with its own weapon, 0.7 m | to make | ACT 1, 3, 5, 6, 8 |
| 4 | @CALDERA | BOSS CALDERA annotated character sheet, height 2.4 m | to make | ACT 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 |
| 5 | @RIDERS | CALDERA'S RIDERS group sheet, 9 mixed creature gunmen in size order | to make | ACT 0-7 |
| 6 | @SIZE | SIZE COMPARISON sheet, all of the above on one ground line with height labels | to make | any clip with 2+ characters |
| 7 | @DUSTHORSE | DUST-HORSE sheet, black variant and grey variant, saddle detail | to make | ACT 0, 2, 3, 4 |
| 8 | @TRUCK | HOVER-TRUCK sheet, 4 m flatbed, thruster pods, water and powder barrels | to make | ACT 0, 2, 3, 6 |
| 9 | @ORGAN | PROP: the pipe organ, front and open-lid view showing the two sawn-offs inside | to make | ACT 1 |
| 10 | @MASK | PROP: the iron grille-mask, close-up, front and three-quarter | to make | every mask CU |
| 11 | @CROSS | PROP: the heavy silver cross on its chain | to make | ACT 1, 7, 8 |
| 12 | @MISSION | LOCATION (recurring): the IRON MISSION exterior, 16:9, no characters | to make | ACT 0 end, ACT 2 end, ACT 8 |
| 13 | @CRYPT | LOCATION (recurring): the crypt wall with twelve cut names, 16:9, lantern lit | to make | ACT 8, and every episode's closing |
| 14 | @PREVIOUS_CLIP | the previous clip, for EXTEND mode only | n/a | every EXTEND |

**Deliberately NOT made:** mission nave interior, bell tower, salt flats, canyon, ghost-town street,
mine bridge, water-fort. All one-visit locations — the act master establishes them and the EXTEND
chain carries them. This is the whole point of the location policy.

## Sheet rules (from the skill, repeated so nothing is lost)
- The prompt states inside itself what the image is FOR ("CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET for a film
  character named ...", "LOCATION REFERENCE for ...", "PROP REFERENCE ...").
- Character sheets are annotated: front / side / back full-body + head close-up + hand close-up,
  small hand-lettered labels naming the parts and the height. Labels are the only text in the image.
- Flat, shadowless lighting, plain mid-grey studio background, photoreal skin and scale texture.
- Group sheets in size order. The size chart is generated with the character sheets attached.
- Location images: one 16:9 view, no characters, no text except in-world signage, filthy west grime,
  everything old, broken, patched and dirty, nothing clean or new.
- The CRYPT image carries the twelve carved names; clip prompts say "copy the carved names exactly"
  and the Avoid line bans any other writing.

# IRON SUNDAY — Music Cue Sheet (Suno, instrumental, Rango vibe)
**Never inside a video prompt.** Every clip's Audio line ends with `No background music.`
Cues are scored in the edit. Silence or ambience before every burst of violence and under every
deadpan gag; fights are SFX-first with the music dropping out on the first shot.

| Cue | Where | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| **MAIN THEME "Iron Sunday"** | ACT 0, over the 45 s ride and credits | Instrumental spaghetti western meets mariachi. Twangy tremolo baritone guitar riff in spring reverb, galloping nylon-string strumming, a mariachi trumpet duo, lonesome whistling, jaw harp, castanets and whip cracks, guitarron bass, a deep male choir shouting hey on the off-beat. 120 bpm, dusty 1960s analog tape, Morricone meets Los Lobos, heroic but mischievous. |
| **THE ORGANIST motif** | ACT 1 opening, ACT 4 (the horse), ACT 8 | A lone whistled melody over tremolo baritone guitar drenched in spring reverb, a distant low male choir, one struck tubular bell. 60 bpm, ominous and lonely, almost no percussion. |
| **CALDERA's theme** | ACT 1 aisle walk, ACT 7 stare-down | Sleazy ranchera swagger. Out-of-tune honky-tonk piano, accordion, guitarron, muted trumpet with a wah slide, lazy shuffling snare, gold-toothed and pleased with itself. 110 bpm. |
| **THE CHOIR gag** | ACT 3 SD-25, ACT 5 SD-39 | Comic mariachi miniature. Three tiny trumpets slightly out of tune with each other, woodblock, jaw harp, a hiccuping tuba, bad ensemble timing on purpose. 100 bpm, 20 seconds, deadpan. |
| **SALT FLATS chase** | ACT 3 | Flamenco rasgueado, galloping snare, blaring mariachi trumpets, surf-twang lead guitar, gang shouts, tambourine. 170 bpm, relentless, no let-up. |
| **CANYON fall** | ACT 4 SD-29 to SD-31 | Everything stops. One musical saw, a single nylon guitar note ringing, low timpani heartbeat, distant wind. 50 bpm, 40 seconds, grief without a melody. |
| **GHOST TOWN walk** | ACT 5 | Ticking pocket-watch percussion, tremolo strings swelling slowly, a solo mariachi trumpet lament, anvil hits on the beat, then a huge held chord and sudden silence. |
| **BRIDGE** | ACT 6 | Driving 6/8 with hand-claps, baritone guitar tremolo, trumpets stabbing on the off-beats, a whip crack every bar, building to one bass-drum hit. 150 bpm. |
| **THE DUEL** | ACT 7 SD-59 to SD-62 | Classic Morricone stand-off. Ticking pocket-watch chimes, a lone ocarina-like whistle, tremolo strings rising, solo trumpet lament, anvil, timpani heartbeat, then complete silence for four bars. 70 bpm. |
| **CRYPT coda** | ACT 8 | Slow nylon guitar arpeggio, musical saw, a muted trumpet answering once, one tubular bell, unresolved final chord that does not land. 60 bpm. |

## Not allowed
Toy piano, nursery or children's-poem style, ukulele, glockenspiel, orchestral trailer hits,
modern drum kit, synth pads. If a cue starts sounding cute, it is wrong for this series.

def merge(path, key, additions):
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data.setdefault(key, {}).update(additions)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    return sorted(additions)


def main():
    added_c = merge(ROOT / "bible" / "characters.json", "characters", CHARACTERS)
    added_l = merge(ROOT / "bible" / "locations.json", "locations", LOCATIONS)

    scope_path = ROOT / "SCOPE_FILMS.json"
    scope = json.loads(scope_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    films = scope.setdefault("films", [])
    if "iron-sunday" not in films:
        films.append("iron-sunday")
    scope_path.write_text(json.dumps(scope, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

    print("characters added:", added_c)
    print("locations added:", added_l)
    print("films:", films)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# IRON SUNDAY — Reference Image Index

**Numbering rule (owner, 2026-09-22).** Reference images stay saved in the tool under a fixed number.
So numbers are assigned **in the order the images are actually created**, starting at Image 1, and are
never changed afterwards. A planned image has no number until the day it is made.
Images are made on demand, clip by clip — never as a batch up front.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| 3 | @TRUCK | HOVER-TRUCK vehicle sheet, 4 views, thruster pod close-up | to make | SD-01 |

|---|---|---|

`@PREVIOUS_CLIP` is not an image — it is the previous clip, attached in EXTEND mode.

## Deliberately never made
Mission nave interior, bell tower, salt flats, canyon, ghost-town street, mine bridge, water-fort.
All one-visit locations — the act master establishes them and the EXTEND chain carries them.
This is the whole point of the location policy.

## Sheet rules
- The prompt states inside itself what the image is FOR ("CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET for a film
  character named ...", "LOCATION REFERENCE for ...", "PROP REFERENCE ...").
- Character sheets are annotated: front / side / back full-body + head close-up + hand close-up,
  with small hand-lettered labels naming the parts and the height. Labels are the only text.
- Flat shadowless lighting, plain mid-grey studio background, photoreal skin and scale texture.
- Group sheets in size order. The size chart is generated with the character sheets attached.
- Location images: one 16:9 view, no characters, no text except in-world signage, filthy west grime,
  everything old, broken, patched and dirty, nothing clean or new.
- The CRYPT image carries the twelve carved names; clip prompts say "copy the carved names exactly"
  and the Avoid line bans any other writing.

# SD-01C me kya ho raha hai

**Film me jagah:** 0:30 se 0:45. Opening ride ka teesra aur aakhri clip. Credits abhi bhi neeche chal rahe hain. Iske foran baad film andar chali jati hai — mission ke andar, jahan organ baj raha hai.

**Kaam kya hai is clip ka:** do cheezein. Ek, gang ko pehli baar *qareeb* se dikhana — pehle 30 second me wo door se aur upar se dikhe the. Do, **jagah introduce karna** — audience ko pehli baar pata chalta hai ki yeh sab kahan ja rahe hain.

### Beat by beat

**0-8 second — zameen wala pass**
Camera zameen pe pada hai, lens bilkul mitti ke barabar, hilta nahi. Door se convoy seedha camera ki taraf aata hai. Pehle chhota, phir tezi se bara hota jata hai. Aakhri do second me ekdum upar se aur bagal se guzar jata hai — split-claw khur zameen pe padte dikhte hain, trucks ke thruster pods chamakte hue nikal jate hain. Unke guzarne ke baad dhool uth-ti hai.

Yeh clip ka "power" shot hai — sabse qareeb audience gang ko is poore sequence me aati hai.

**8-15 second — peeche se drone**
Cut. Ab camera convoy ke peeche, oonchai pe, unke saath aage badh raha hai. Convoy frame ke neeche beech me tikaa rehta hai. Unke saamne ufaq pe **IRON MISSION** dikhta hai — chhota, phir dheere dheere bara hota hua. Akela building, khali desert me, bell tower safed aasman ke khilaaf. Ghodon aur trucks ke peeche lambi dhool ki lakeerein.

Clip yahin khatam — mission abhi door hai, andar nahi gaye.

### Awaaz
Khur ki awaaz pehle door, phir camera ke paas aate hi zor ki, phir peeche jaati hui. Truck ka diesel drone, saddle ki chamdi, saans, hawa, dhool. **Koi music nahi** — wo tum editor me lagaoge.

---

## Jo cheezein is clip me badalna aasaan hai — bolo to badal dun

1. **Pass kis taraf se ho** — abhi camera ke upar se aur bagal se. Chaho to sirf bagal se (safe), ya bilkul upar se (zyada dramatic, lekin model kabhi kabhi ghodon ki tangein ajeeb bana deta hai).
2. **Mission kitna door dikhe** — abhi dur, chhota. Chaho to zyada qareeb kar dun taake building saaf dikhe, lekin phir SD-02 ka andar jaana kam surprise rehta hai.
3. **Cut kahan ho** — abhi 8 second pe. 10 pe kar dun to ground pass lamba, drone chhota.
4. **Do moons** — abhi is clip me hain. Nikalwa dun to frame aur saaf ho jayega.
5. **Aakhri second** — abhi sirf mission dikhta hai. Chaho to mission ke darwaze ke upar ek jhulta hua zang-khaya cross add kar dun — ek chhoti si detail jo baad me matlab rakhti hai.

# Is clip me kya hoga

**Film me jagah:** 1:00 se 1:30. Ride khatam, pehli baar hum andar hain. Yeh **ACT 1 ka master** hai — is ke baad ke saare clips isi ko EXTEND karke banenge, isliye kamra, roshni aur sab ki positions yahin se set hoti hain.

**0-8 s — kamra.** Camera church ke pichhle hisse se, pew ki oonchai pe, bohot dheere aisle me aage badhta hai. Dono taraf tooti hui benchein, khirkiyon ki darar se dhool ke teekhe shafts, aakhir me organ aur us pe ek amber lamp. ORGANIST peeth kiye baitha baja raha hai. Aur kuch nahi hilta. Yeh 8 second audience ko jagah samjhane ke liye hain.

**8-14 s — darwaza.** Cut. Ab camera organ ke paas se peeche darwaze ki taraf dekh raha hai. Darwaza laat se khulta hai aur deewar se takrata hai. Safed dhoop ka ek wedge poore aisle me girta hai, dhool us roshni me ubalti hai. Chhe gunmen andar aate hain aur dono taraf phail jate hain, bandooken uthi hui. Phir ruk jate hain.

**14-22 s — Caldera.** Cut. Camera uske saath chalta hai jab wo aisle ke beech se organ ki taraf aata hai. Dheere chalta hai, gold daant ki muskurahat, zubaan nikalti hui, chaandi ka cross seene pe jhoolta hua. Dono taraf uske aadmi jame khade hain. Wo ek line bolta hai: *"You are in my church, friend."*

**22-30 s — do log, ek frame.** Cut. Bagal se medium shot. Caldera baithe hue ORGANIST ke bilkul peeche aa kar rukta hai, us pe chhaya jaisa khada, aur apna chaura haath organ ke upar lamp ke barabar rakh deta hai. ORGANIST na mudta hai, na dekhta hai, na bajana band karta hai. Clip yahin ruk jati hai.

**Awaaz:** organ poore 30 second chalta rehta hai — do note bajte hi nahi, sirf click karte hain. Hawa, darwaze ka dhamaka, boot aur spurs, ek shotgun cock hone ki awaaz, Caldera ke bhaari qadam aur uski ek line. Aur koi nahi bolta.

## Jo badal sakte ho
1. **Caldera ki line** — abhi *"You are in my church, friend."* Nikal bhi sakti hai; phir poora clip bilkul khamosh rahega sirf organ ke saath, jo aur bhaari lagega. Bolo to hata dun.
2. **Muskurahat** — abhi grin hai, hansi nahi (tumhari baat yaad hai). Chaho to bilkul bhaav-heen kar dun.
3. **Chhe gunmen** — chaar kar dun to frame saaf rahega aur drift kam hoga.
4. **Aakhri shot ka haath** — abhi organ ke upar haath rakhta hai. Isse zyada tez chahiye to haath ORGANIST ke kandhe pe rakhwa dun — lekin phir agla clip (uska palat kar dekhna) zyada bhaari ho jayega.
5. **Size chart** — do lambe kirdar ek frame me hain (2.2 vs 2.4 m). Agar pehle render me unki lambai galat aaye to main ek size-comparison sheet ka prompt de dunga aur wo image8 ban jayegi.

## 1. MAIN THEME — opening ride (0:00-1:00)

```
Instrumental spaghetti-western main theme with a Mexican mariachi heart, in the spirit of a dusty 1960s Morricone score crossed with Los Lobos. 120 BPM, key of D minor, recorded to warm analog tape with natural room reverb and light tape saturation. Core sound: a twangy tremolo baritone electric guitar drenched in spring reverb carrying the main riff, fast galloping nylon-string acoustic strumming underneath, a pair of mariachi trumpets in close harmony answering the guitar, a lonesome whistled melody, jaw harp, castanets, a deep guitarron bass line, tambourine, and a whip crack on the downbeat of every fourth bar.

At 0:08 the galloping nylon guitar and guitarron enter together and lock into a hard riding groove. At 0:20 the twangy baritone guitar states the main riff. At 0:32 the mariachi trumpets take the melody over the guitar, bigger and prouder. At 0:45 everything drops to just percussion, jaw harp and whip cracks for four bars, then the full band returns for a final statement of the riff and ends on one long ringing chord at 1:00.
Mood: heroic, dangerous and mischievous, dry and sun-bleached, a gang riding hard across a desert. Instrumental only, no sung lyrics and no words; whistling and short wordless shouted male gang calls are the only voices.
```

# IRON SUNDAY — Music Cue Sheet
**Tool: ElevenLabs Music v2.5** (owner, 2026-09-23). Prompts are written as natural-language
descriptions with a timed structure, which this model follows better than short tag lists.
Always set the length explicitly rather than leaving it on Auto.

**Never put music inside a video prompt.** Every clip's Audio line ends with `No background music.`
Cues are added in the edit.

## The scoring rule for this series
Silence before every burst of violence; noise after it. A cue starts ON the first shot, never before.
Deadpan beats play dry with sound effects only. If a cue would cover a silence that the scene is
built on, the silence wins.

| Where music runs | Where it does not |
|---|---|
| the opening ride and credits | the mission nave until the first shotgun blast |
| from the first shot of each gunfight | the six seconds of silence in SD-03 |
| the canyon loss, the ghost-town walk, the stare-down, the crypt | any moment the organ is playing |

---

```
Instrumental spaghetti-western main theme with a Mexican mariachi heart, in the spirit of a dusty 1960s Morricone score crossed with Los Lobos. 120 BPM, key of D minor, recorded to warm analog tape with natural room reverb and light tape saturation. Structure over 60 seconds: start at 0:00 with four bars of solo whistling over one sustained tremolo guitar note and distant wind. At 0:08 the galloping nylon guitar and guitarron enter together and lock into a hard riding groove. At 0:20 the twangy baritone guitar states the main riff. At 0:32 the mariachi trumpets take the melody over the guitar, bigger and prouder. At 0:45 everything drops to just percussion, jaw harp and whip cracks for four bars, then the full band returns for a final statement of the riff and ends on one long ringing chord at 1:00.
```

## 3. THE ORGANIST motif — the mask, the crypt, 40 s
```
Instrumental spaghetti-western character motif for a masked silent gunman. 60 BPM, key of A minor, very sparse, warm analog tape with long spring reverb and a wide empty stereo field. Core sound: one lonesome whistled melody carrying the theme, a tremolo baritone electric guitar holding long sustained notes underneath, a distant low male choir humming one wordless chord, a single struck tubular bell, and faint desert wind. Almost no percussion, only one soft timpani heartbeat every two bars.
Structure over 40 seconds: 0:00 wind and one guitar note alone. 0:06 the whistled melody enters and states the theme once. 0:18 the low choir fades in beneath it. 0:26 one tubular bell strike, then the whistle repeats the theme lower and slower. Ends at 0:40 on an unresolved chord that does not settle.
Mood: lonely, patient and ominous, the sound of something that cannot be talked out of what it is doing. Instrumental only, no sung lyrics and no words; only whistling and wordless humming.
```

## 4. CALDERA's theme — his swagger, 30 s
```
Instrumental sleazy Mexican ranchera swagger for a fat gold-toothed outlaw boss. 110 BPM, key of G major, warm analog tape, slightly out of tune on purpose. Core sound: an out-of-tune honky-tonk upright piano, a wheezing accordion, guitarron bass walking lazily, a muted trumpet sliding into its notes with a wah effect, a loose shuffling snare with brushes, and a woodblock.
Structure over 30 seconds: 0:00 piano and accordion start mid-phrase as if already playing. 0:08 the guitarron and shuffle enter. 0:16 the muted trumpet takes the melody with sliding wah notes. 0:26 the band slows down and stops on one flat sour chord.
Mood: pleased with itself, greasy, dangerous but ridiculous. Instrumental only, no sung lyrics and no words.
```

## 5. THE CHOIR gag — the comic chorus, 20 s
```
Instrumental comic mariachi miniature for three small clumsy characters. 100 BPM, key of C major, dry and close-recorded. Core sound: three small trumpets playing the same simple fanfare slightly out of tune with each other and slightly out of time, a hiccuping tuba on the bass notes, woodblock, jaw harp, and a single triangle ping at the end.
Structure over 20 seconds: 0:00 the three trumpets attempt a proud fanfare and do not quite line up. 0:08 the tuba enters late and plays one wrong note. 0:12 they try the fanfare again, better but still wrong. 0:19 one triangle ping, then silence.
Mood: deadpan, silly, played completely straight. Instrumental only, no sung lyrics and no words.
```

## 6. CANYON LOSS — the horse dies, 40 s
```
Instrumental desert lament for a moment of loss, in the spaghetti-western tradition. 50 BPM, key of D minor, very sparse and quiet, warm analog tape, wide empty stereo field with distant wind. Core sound: a bowed musical saw carrying a slow wavering melody, one nylon-string guitar note ringing and decaying, a low timpani heartbeat, a faint sustained string pad far back in the mix, and no percussion of any other kind.
Structure over 40 seconds: 0:00 wind alone. 0:05 one guitar note. 0:10 the musical saw enters with the melody, slow and unsteady. 0:24 the timpani heartbeat begins underneath. 0:34 the saw holds one long note and fades out with the wind at 0:40.
Mood: grief without drama, dust and heat, nothing resolved. Instrumental only, no sung lyrics and no words.
```

## 7. GHOST-TOWN WALK — the street approach, 40 s
```
Instrumental spaghetti-western tension cue for a lone gunman walking down an empty street. 90 BPM, key of E minor, warm analog tape, long stone reverb. Core sound: a ticking pocket watch as the percussion, slowly swelling tremolo strings, a solo mariachi trumpet playing a lonesome lament, anvil strikes on the beat, a low timpani heartbeat, and a tremolo baritone guitar holding one long note.
Structure over 40 seconds: 0:00 the ticking watch alone. 0:06 the baritone guitar note and anvil enter. 0:14 the solo trumpet plays the lament. 0:26 the tremolo strings begin to swell and keep rising. 0:36 everything arrives on one huge held chord, then cuts to complete silence at 0:40.
Mood: a countdown, unbearable patience, violence about to happen. Instrumental only, no sung lyrics and no words.
```

## 8. THE DUEL — water-fort stand-off, 50 s
```
Instrumental classic spaghetti-western stand-off cue. 70 BPM, key of A minor, warm analog tape, huge natural reverb. Core sound: ticking pocket-watch chimes, a lone high ocarina-like whistle, tremolo strings rising slowly in pitch and volume, a solo mariachi trumpet lament, anvil strikes, a timpani heartbeat quickening, and a tremolo baritone guitar underneath.
Structure over 50 seconds: 0:00 watch ticks and one whistle note. 0:10 the trumpet states a short lament. 0:20 tremolo strings begin rising and do not stop. 0:32 the timpani heartbeat speeds up and the anvil strikes double. 0:42 everything reaches the top and holds one enormous chord. 0:47 total silence for the last three seconds.
Mood: dread stretched as far as it will go. Instrumental only, no sung lyrics and no words.
```

## 9. CRYPT CODA — the closing shot of every episode, 40 s
```
Instrumental spaghetti-western closing cue, quiet and unresolved. 60 BPM, key of A minor, warm analog tape, long stone reverb. Core sound: a slow fingerpicked nylon-string guitar arpeggio, a bowed musical saw answering it, a muted trumpet playing one short phrase, a single struck tubular bell, and faint underground drips and wind.
Structure over 40 seconds: 0:00 the guitar arpeggio begins alone. 0:10 the musical saw answers. 0:20 the muted trumpet plays its one phrase. 0:30 the tubular bell strikes once and the guitar plays a final chord that does not resolve, ringing out to 0:40.
Mood: patient, cold, unfinished, eleven names left. Instrumental only, no sung lyrics and no words.
```

## Never
Toy piano, nursery or children's style, ukulele, glockenspiel, orchestral trailer hits, modern drum
kit, synth pads, sung lyrics. If a cue starts sounding cute, it is wrong for this series.

## Kaunse tareeqe daale hain aur kyun

**1. 180-degree line — sabse bara.** Asli filmon me camera action ki ek hi taraf rehta hai, warna log screen pe jagah badalte mehsoos hote hain chahe kuch bhi na badla ho. Prompt me isko aise likha hai jo model samajh sake: *"daylight hamesha frame ke baaen se, amber lamp hamesha daaen, organ hamesha door, darwaze hamesha camera ke peeche."* Ab screen direction palat nahi sakti.

**2. Roshni ka qanoon, har shot me wahi.** Sirf **do** light sources, kitne hain yeh ginti likhi hai, kis taraf se aate hain likha hai, aur jo un tak nahi pahunchti wo **kaali** rehti hai. Roshni ka side badalna continuity ka sabse zyada nazar aane wala toot-na hai, aur model bina roke yeh karta hai.

**3. Har shot me ek anchor.** Har coverage shot me wo cheez maujood hai jo master me thi — organ ka case, amber lamp. Aankh continuity us cheez se padhti hai aur kamre ka hisaab lagana chhod deti hai.

**4. Kisi cheez ke saamne shoot karo, khali kamre me nahi.** Darwaze wala shot sirf darwazon pe hai. Caldera wala shot uske kandhe ke saath hai. Aakhri shot itna tight hai ki peeche kuch padha hi nahi ja sakta. **Khali kamre me dekhta hua shot model ko kamra dobara banane ki dawat hai.**

**5. Shallow focus + kaala background.** Saaf likha hai: subject sharp, peecha ghor beghor aur andhere me. Jo audience resolve nahi kar sakti, wo badalta hua pakad bhi nahi sakti.

**6. Frame me jagah fix.** Aakhri shot me Organist hamesha **baaen**, Caldera hamesha **daaen**. Eyelines milti hain, koi side badalta mehsoos nahi hota.

**7. Har cut harkat pe.** "Cut on the first bang of the doors", "cut as the last one clears the frame", "cut as he plants his hand". Vyast aankh geometry ka audit nahi karti.

**8. Look block ab canonical hai.** ACT 1 ke har agle clip me **yehi alfaz, hu-ba-hu** copy honge. Alag lafzon me kamra dobara likhna model ko kamra dobara ijaad karne pe majboor karta hai — pichhli baar yahi hua.

**9. Farsh aur chhat kam.** Sab framings chest-to-head hain. Zyada farsh aur chhat matlab model ke paas ijaad karne ki jagah.

**10. Ending qata'i.** 28 s pe organ **rukta hai**, do keys click, dono gloved haath keyboard pe, sab still, khamoshi me khatam. Extend ke paas ab ek hi saaf cheez hai jahan se shuru ho.

---

Yeh dus rules file me save kar diye hain, ab har interior scene pe apne aap lagenge.

Render ho jaye to batao **aakhri frame me asal me kya dikh raha hai** — khaas kar Caldera ka haath kahan hai, Organist ke haath keys pe hain ya nahi, aur lamp kis taraf hai. Usi se SD-03 ka pehla jumla likhunga.

Faisla mera hai to main **15 second** chun raha hoon, aur apna pichhla "30 s default" wala rule wapas le raha hoon. Wajah saaf hai:

**30 second aur 4,000 character ki limit ek saath chal hi nahi sakte.** Jo cheezein drift rokti hain — do-light rule, 180-degree line, har shot ka anchor, shallow focus, frame positions — wo jagah mangti hain. 30 s me char shots likhne ke baad in sab ko kaatna padta hai, aur wahi cheez kat-ti hai jo render ko bachati hai. Pichhla 30 s extend isi wajah se fail hua tha, seams ki wajah se nahi.

Aur do faide: fail hone pe aadhe credits jate hain, aur 15 s me sirf do shots hote hain to model ke paas ghalti karne ki jagah kam hoti hai.

# Is clip me kya hoga

**0-8 s — khamoshi.** Seedha mask pe. Kaale shishe ki darar me amber lamp ka ek nuqta. Caldera daaen taraf sirf ek dhundhla kaala saya. Chhe second kuch nahi hota — phir **sar ek degree hilta hai.** Bas itna. Cut.

**8-14 s — hathiyar.** Organ ke case pe insert. Gauntlet gloves dhakkan uthate hain, peetal ke paipon me se do sawn-off nikalte hain, dhakkan girta hai, dono nalliyan load ho kar band. Cut.

**14-22 s — pehla khoon.** Organist bench se poori lambai me khada hota hai, palat-ta hai, ek nalli chalata hai. Muzzle flash dhool ko chamka deta hai. **TUSK** — bhaari boar — pew ke upar se peeche gir kar frame se neeche gayab. Cut.

**22-30 s — fight shuru.** Caldera organ ke peeche jhuk jata hai, lamp uske upar hilta hai. Organist baaen taraf dono bandooken uthaye khada. Peeche, andhere me aur focus se bahar, paanch gunmen bikhar kar firing shuru karte hain. Dhool ke shafts me flashes aur dhuan.

**Awaaz:** pehle 6 second sirf hawa. Phir lakdi, steel, do cartridge. Phir **ek bohot bara dhamaka** pathar se goonjta hua. Uske baad jawabi fire aur peetal ke paipon pe lagti goliyan.

=== ASSISTANT 2026-09-22T22:03 ===
Bilkul samajh gaya. Apne alfaz me dohra deta hoon taake koi shak na rahe:

1. **Ek kirdar, tang frame → chhota clip (10 s) theek hai.** Organist akela organ baja raha hai, na darwaza dikh raha hai, na kamra — kuch bhi drift karne ke liye hai hi nahi.
2. **Wide shot sirf 30 s wale clip me aayega.** Hard cut, aur 30 s ka clip wahan se shuru jab darwaza dharam se khulta hai.
3. **Entry aur poori fight usi 30 s ke andar khatam.** Ek location, multiple characters = ek hi 30 s generation.
4. **Agar baad me extend karna pare to wo kabhi wide nahi hoga** — tang shots, aur koshish yeh ki zaroorat hi na pare.
5. 6-8 minute ki film me 30 second bohot hota hai — ek poori scene us me khatam honi chahiye.

Yeh isliye sahi hai ki masla seams ka nahi tha — masla **geometry** ka tha. Jahan geometry frame me hai (wide, multiple log), wahan sab kuch ek generation me hona chahiye. Jahan geometry hai hi nahi (akela kirdar, tang shot), wahan clip chhota aur sasta ho sakta hai.

## Is clip me kya hoga
Das second, ek hi shot, koi cut nahi. Camera uske baaen kandhe ke peeche se shuru hota hai — bilkul tight, sirf kaale gauntlet gloves peele pade keys pe chal rahe hain, daaen taraf amber lamp jal raha hai. Uske peeche sab kuch focus se bahar aur qareeban kaala hai.

Wo bina ruke bajata rehta hai. Frame me dhool ke siwa kuch nahi hilta.

**Yeh clip jaan bujh kar "khali" hai** — ismein koi geometry nahi, isliye ismein kuch bigar bhi nahi sakta. Aur audience ko pehla ehsaas yeh milta hai ki koi aadmi akela, andhere me, ek toote hue organ pe baj raha hai. Uske foran baad darwaza toot-ta hai.

# Is 30 s me kya hoga

| Time | Kya |
|---|---|
| **0-6 s** | **Poori film ka akela wide.** Darwaza dharam se khulta hai, safed dhoop aisle me girti hai, dhool ubalti hai. Chhe gunmen andar aa kar benchon ke beech phail jate hain, Caldera unke peeche. Door organ pe Organist peeth kiye baja raha hai |
| **6-12 s** | Camera Caldera ke saath. Peecha kaala aur blur. Gold daant, zubaan, jhoolta cross. Organ pe haath rakhta hai — *"You are in my church, friend."* |
| **12-17 s** | Mask ka close-up. Slit me lamp ka nuqta. **Organ rukta hai**, do keys click. Sar ek degree hilta hai |
| **17-21 s** | Organ ke case pe insert. Gloves dhakkan uthate hain, do sawn-off nikalte hain, load, band |
| **21-26 s** | Organist khada hota hai, palat-ta hai, fire. **TUSK** pew ke upar. Dusri nalli — **CARRION** gir jata hai. Caldera organ ke peeche jhuk jata hai |
| **26-30 s** | Wo aisle me aage badhta hai, reload karte hue. Ek aur fire — **FANG** gir jata hai. Door, dhundhla: **Caldera, DUNE, MANGE, SKITTER** pichhle darwaze se nikal jate hain. Darwaza khali jhool raha hai. Wo chalta rehta hai |

**Teen marte hain, teen bhagte hain** — aur teeno alag-alag lamhon me, apne apne naam se. Yeh wo cheez hai jo pichhli baar sabse zyada kharab hui thi.

=== ASSISTANT 2026-09-22T22:32 ===
Frame dekh liya. Yeh meri ghalti hai, skill ki nahi — maine shot 4 me "tight on THE ORGANIST" likha lekin shot 1 ke wide me sab ko ek saath khada kar diya tha, aur model ne wahi composition poore clip me pakde rakhi. Jab ek baar sab ek frame me aa jaate hain, model unhe alag nahi karta.

Tumhara rule bilkul sahi hai aur yeh reference channel bhi yahi karta hai — Wanted Reloaded me **dushman kabhi ek frame me nahi hote**. Fight = akele chehron ki katai: shooter lens ki taraf aim karta hai → cut → victim girta hai. Yehi Leone ka tareeqa hai. Aur iska ek bara faida hai jo tumhare consistency masle ko bhi hal karta hai:

**Jis shot me ek hi kirdar hai, us me koi geometry hai hi nahi jo drift kare.** Isliye fight ke shots ko ek 30 s generation me hona zaroori nahi — har kill apna alag 10 s clip ho sakta hai, sasta, aur ek doosre se takraane ki koi jagah nahi. 30 s sirf **setup** ke liye (wide entry, Caldera ki chaal, mask, shotguns) — fight shuru hone se pehle khatam.

## Arrows / storyboard ka seedha jawab
Nahi. Teen wajah:
1. **Storyboard sheet is project me pehle test ho chuki hai aur fail hui** (SIX COFFINS, rule 11 me likha hai). Model frames ko instruction nahi, tasveer samajhta hai.
2. **Blocking image (image14) generate hi nahi hui** — kal dekha.
3. **Arrows** usi family ki cheez hai: model ya to arrows render kar deta hai, ya nazar-andaz. Credits ka nuksan.

Masla reference images se nahi, **shot structure** se hal hota hai. Ek kirdar per frame = kuch bhi galat nahi ho sakta.

## Yeh kyun kaam karega
- **SD-C1 me kabhi do log ek frame me nahi.** Shot 1 sirf Organist, shot 2 sirf TUSK. Model ke paas galat karne ko kuch hai hi nahi.
- **Direction hi geography hai.** Organist right ki taraf fire karta hai, TUSK left se lagta hai. Audience ko dono ek saath dikhaye bagair pata hai kya hua.
- **SD-C2 aur SD-C3 isi template ki copy hain** — sirf victim ki sheet aur uske girne ka tareeqa badlega (CARRION khirki ke neeche dhair, FANG pew se tak-ra kar). Chaho to abhi likh doon, lekin pehle SD-C1 render karke dekho ki pattern chalta hai — phir baaki do pe credits lagao.
- **SD-C4** (Caldera + 2 gunmen ka bhagna) me teen kirdar honge, lekin sab ek team — tumhare rule ke mutabiq allowed.

Rule 20 file me likh diya hai, storyboard/arrows/blocking-image ke "nahi" samet.

=== USER 2026-09-22T22:38 ===
Dont you think har clip k andr characters ki position change hogi?

=== ASSISTANT 2026-09-22T22:38 ===
Haan — **badlegi.** Model kisi clip me kisi ka exact spot yaad nahi rakhega. Main yeh chhupa nahi raha. Lekin asal sawal yeh hai: **kya audience ko wo tabdeeli nazar aayegi?** Aur jawab hai nahi — agar frame me compare karne ke liye kuch hai hi nahi.

Yeh koi AI trick nahi, 100 saal purani editing hai. Jab tum ek akele aadmi ka shot dekhte ho, phir cut, phir doosre akele aadmi ka shot — tumhara dimaag khud faisla karta hai ki wo ek doosre ke saamne khade hain. Kamra dikhana zaroori nahi. Leone ke duel me kabhi teen log ek wide me nahi hote fire ke waqt; sirf aankhein, haath, holster — aur tum phir bhi jaante ho kaun kahan hai.

## Audience asal me kya check karti hai (aur yahi chaar cheezein match honi chahiye)

| Cheez | Kaise pakki hoti hai |
|---|---|
| **Screen direction** | Organist hamesha right ki taraf, gang hamesha left ki taraf. Yeh ek baar galat hua to poora fight ulta lagta hai — isliye har prompt me likha hai |
| **Anchor object** | Organist ke peeche hamesha organ + amber lamp. Gunman ke peeche hamesha ek tooti pew. Aankh "organ = wahi jagah" padhti hai, exact spot nahi |
| **Roshni ka rukh** | Daylight hamesha left se. Roshni palat gayi to dimaag foran kehta hai "jagah badal gayi" |
| **Shot size** | Dono medium, chest height. Ek wide aur ek close ke beech cut pe dimaag jagah ka hisaab lagane lagta hai |

Yeh chaar theek hain to absolute position ka koi matlab nahi. TUSK wide me "baaen taraf, doosri pew ke paas" tha; SD-C1 me wo "ek tooti pew ke saamne" hai. Koi nahi kahega ki wo hil gaya — kyunki pew pew hai.

## Jahan yeh TOOTEGA — aur isliye structure aisa hai
1. **Wide → medium cut.** Wide ke foran baad kisi ka medium aaye to dimaag ke paas abhi kamre ka naqsha taaza hota hai aur wo compare karta hai. Isliye SD-B me wide sirf pehle 8 s hai, phir Caldera ka tracking (7 s), phir mask (7 s), phir haath (8 s) — wide aur fight ke beech **22 second tight shots** hain. Naqsha dimaag se mit chuka hota hai jab tak SD-C1 aata hai.
2. **Edit ki tarteeb.** Victim ka shot hamesha shooter ke baad cut karo, kabhi wide ke baad nahi. Yeh editor me tumhara kaam hai.
3. **Do log ek frame me.** Jahan do dushman ek frame me hain, wahan geometry frame me hai aur compare hoti hai. Isliye rule 20.

Ek line me: **positions ko rokne ki koshish chhod do — unhe dikhne se roko.** Yehi wo cheez hai jo pichhle teen fail renders ne sikhai.

=== ASSISTANT 2026-09-23T01:53 ===
Teeno baatein sahi hain aur teeno meri galti. Rules me daal raha hoon, phir dono clips theek.

**1. Figurative alfaz.** "swinging open onto white glare", "shoves through", "is gone", "walks into the glare", "ducking under the lintel" — AI ko yeh sab literal chahiye: *"the door is open. Bright daylight comes through it. CALDERA walks through the door and out. He is no longer visible."* Bas.

**2. Mare hue log wapas aa gaye.** CARRION shot 1 me gira, aakhir me bhaag raha tha aur zameen pe bhi tha — kyunki maine ek shot me chaar gang members blur me daal diye aur naam bina tag ke the. Ab: **har mention pe @image tag**, har shot me saaf list **kaun frame me hai aur kaun nahi**, aur Avoid me "the fallen do not appear again."

**3. "Turns back toward the organ"** — bekaar ka mod. Geography aisi banata hoon ki mudna hi na pade: Organist organ ke paas hi khada reh kar fire karta hai, Caldera ka pichhla darwaza organ ke bilkul saath hai — do qadam, koi turn nahi. Bache hue teen door wale main door se bhagte hain.

Teen baatein sahi hain, aur teeno ka hal alag hai:

1. **Extend faida nahi de raha** — kyunki main seam pe foran HARD CUT kar deta tha. Extend tab kaam karta hai jab uska pehla shot pichhle clip ke aakhri shot ko *usi frame me* chand second aage chalaye, phir cut ho. Main yeh galat kar raha tha.
2. **Laashein dikhni chahiye** — haan, meri zyadti thi. "Not in any later shot" hata kar "lies still in the background" hoga.
3. **Template** — sahi kaha. Main apna structure bana raha tha. Pehle skill me jo do tutorials study hue the unka asli template padhta hoon, phir Higgsfield ka Seedance 2.5 guide dhoondhta hoon, aur usi pe likhta hoon.

# Higgsfield official Seedance 2.5 prompt template (adopted 2026-09-24)

Source: Higgsfield, "Seedance 2.5: Complete Prompting Guide (Full Prompt Library)",
https://higgsfield.ai/blog/seedance-2-5-prompting-guide (read 2026-09-24). Extend wording from
Morphic, https://morphic.com/resources/how-to/seedance-2-5-guide. Failure modes cross-checked
against https://www.heyuan110.com/posts/ai/2026-07-11-seedance-2-prompt-guide/.
This is now the house template for every Seedance 2.5 clip. The owner asked for it after the
home-grown structure kept failing (2026-09-24).

## Section order (all ten, in this order, one continuous block, labelled)

```
GLOBAL STYLE: genre, colour grade, film stock/grain, aspect, duration, exclusions.
SCENE: one-line logline — what happens, where, the mood.
CHARACTERS: every character, identity locked to its reference ("@image N, identity and wardrobe
  locked to the reference, ignore the reference backdrop"); which reference is which; "exactly N
  characters, never N+1".
LOCATION: the space and props, separate from people; no readable text.
FIRST FRAME AND BLOCKING: camera position, every character's starting position and facing,
  screen direction ("THE MAN always screen-LEFT, THE WOMAN always screen-RIGHT, they never swap").
Shot 1 (0.0s to 3.0s): shot type, camera, action in order, timing to the tenth of a second. Hard cut.
Shot 2 (3.0s to 7.2s): ... Hard cut.
...
OPTICS: field of view per shot, camera height, dolly/locked/handheld per shot.
PHYSICS: how dust, cloth, smoke, bodies, doors, liquids actually move; real mass and inertia.
LIGHTING: the sources, their number, direction and quality; what stays dark.
AUDIO: ambience, foley with visible sources, dialogue language, timing; what must not appear
  ("No music, no narration").
POSITIVE LOCKS: everything restated as a rule — member count, same face/wardrobe/state across all
  shots "zero drift", geography hold, screen direction, who is hit and stays down, no blood, no
  attached image as a still frame.
```

Rules the guide states outright:
- Timestamps on every shot, to the tenth of a second; "Hard cut" closes every shot.
- Vague location = the most common cause of drift between cuts. Blocking must be exact.
- Screen direction must be stated and held.
- Say what must NOT appear (negative locks) and say it again in POSITIVE LOCKS.
- State the member count as "exactly N, never N+1".
- One continuous block; skipping a section fails in a predictable way.
- Fewer, deliberate references beat a cluttered set; every reference gets an explicit job.

## Extend prompts (Morphic / Higgsfield wording)

Open with the boundary, not with a cut:

```
Extend @Video 1 forward by <N> seconds. The first frame continues directly from the last frame of
@Video 1: same shot, same camera, <who is where, facing which way, what the light is>. Hold this
shot for <2-3> seconds, then Hard cut.
```
The seam only works if the first new shot IS the last old shot continuing. A hard cut on the first
frame throws the continuity away. Then the ten sections as above; CHARACTERS and LOCATION may be
short ("as in @Video 1, locked") but the blocking is restated in full.

## Failure modes (heyuan110), kept because they match our renders
- Instruction overflow: too many demands, half honoured at random -> prioritise, trim.
- Naked references: an untasked reference bleeds its framing/light into the shot -> give each a job.
- Stacked camera moves in one shot -> one move per shot.
- Scene cramming -> scale complexity to duration.

Maine asal template padha, apna structure chhoda, aur dono clips ab **Higgsfield ke official Seedance 2.5 template** pe likhe hain. Dono 4,000 ke andar hain: **IN-01 3,961 · IN-02 3,968**.

## Template se kya mila (aur hum kahan galat the)
- **Das section, isi tarteeb me:** GLOBAL STYLE → SCENE → CHARACTERS → LOCATION → **FIRST FRAME AND BLOCKING** → Shot 1, 2… (timestamps ke saath, har shot "Hard cut" pe khatam) → OPTICS → PHYSICS → LIGHTING → AUDIO → **POSITIVE LOCKS**.
- **Timestamps zaroori hain.** Guide unhe second ke dasve hisse tak likhne ko kehti hai, isliye jo test maine timestamps hata kar chalaya tha wo band.
- **Extend mera galat tha.** Extend ka pehla shot pichhle clip ka **aakhri shot hi** hona chahiye, chand second aage chalta hua: *"The first frame continues directly from the last frame of @Video 1: same shot…"* Main pehle hi frame pe cut kar deta tha, isliye join nahi ban raha tha. Ab IN-02 TUSK wale shot ko **2 second** chalata hai, phir cut karta hai.
- **Laashein dikhti rahengi.** Lock ab yeh hai: *"lie still where they fell and stay visible; never stand"*. Pehle "later shots me nahi dikhenge" likha tha, wo zaroorat se zyada sakht tha.

Dono tayyar, limit ke andar aur tag format check kiya hua: **IN-01 3,972 · IN-02 3,973.** Koi tag bracket me nahi hai, har `@image N` ke dono taraf space hai.

Rules me yeh sab save hai (rule 33):
- **Extend kabhi nahi.** Har clip NEW hoga, joint editor me hard cut se.
- **Tag format:** `TUSK @image 10 lies…`, dono taraf space, bracket nahi.
- **Koi character gayab nahi hoga.** Caldera ab fire ke waqt Organist ke bagal me organ se chipak kar jhukta hai.
- **Organist tez hai.** Dono haath me shotgun, reload ek jhatke me 2 second se kam, har kill 1.5 s.
- **Director ka cutting grammar:** cut on action, shooter/target shot-reverse-shot, 180 line, chase me screen direction (right se nikla to agle shot me left se aayega), 30-degree rule, state match, inserts, sound bridge.
